title: plymeld config
description: plymeld's config. Generated from plymeld-config Schema.kt by `plymeld schema`; do not edit.

$schema.description: the schema an editor checks this file against (ignored by plymeld)

like.description: start from another machine's values (the key of a machine)

model.description: the printer model it is, by the key of a model: one plymeld ships (generic-klipper, qidi-q2, flashforge-c5) or one you describe (hardware.model.<key>): its g-code commands, head shape, and default g-code dialect; several machines may be the same model (the key of a model)

x.description: printable width (X) — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

y.description: printable depth (Y) — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

z.description: printable height (Z) — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

speed.description: fastest printing move (the maker's print speed; travel has motion.travel.speed): hidden lines (inner walls, infill, solid, support) print at it unless the filament's melt rate caps them first, and no printing move goes faster — a speed (mm/s); or a formula (= ...)

acceleration.description: acceleration of printing moves — a accel (mm/s2); or a formula (= ...)

max.description: highest acceleration: what formulas read (the first-use setup writes the print and travel accelerations as formulas of it); nothing else reads it directly: time predictions take the print and travel accelerations from the config, the rest from the machine description — a accel (mm/s2); or a formula (= ...)
fastest Z move (Klipper's [printer] max_z_velocity), for time predictions; unset = its model's — a speed (mm/s); or a formula (= ...)
highest Z acceleration (Klipper's [printer] max_z_accel), for time predictions; unset = its model's — a accel (mm/s2); or a formula (= ...)

speed.description: speed kept through a square corner (Klipper's [printer] square_corner_velocity), for time predictions; unset = its model's — a speed (mm/s); or a formula (= ...)
speed of moves that do not print — a speed (mm/s); or a formula (= ...)

acceleration.description: acceleration of moves that do not print — a accel (mm/s2); or a formula (= ...)

speed.description: the machine's default speed of everything on the first layer, for a filament that sets none of its own (hardware.filament.<key>.motion.first_layer.speed); unset = plymeld's stand-in (plan.mechanism.motion.first_layer.speed in its bundled defaults) — a speed (mm/s); or a formula (= ...)

the speed this machine lays a visible line (outer walls, top and bottom surfaces) at without ringing, as its motion plate measured it (`plymeld calibrate motion values` writes it); used for plan.mechanism.motion.visible.speed unless a config of yours sets that; unset = plymeld's stand-in — a speed (mm/s); or a formula (= ...)

acceleration.description: the acceleration this machine lays a visible line at without ringing, as its motion plate measured it; used for plan.mechanism.motion.visible.acceleration unless a config of yours sets that; unset = plymeld's stand-in — a accel (mm/s2); or a formula (= ...)

flavor.description: the firmware family its g-code is written for

dialect.description: the comments and acceleration command its files are written with, as the maker's own files for its printers have them (flashforge: `;LAYER_CHANGE`, `;TYPE:`, SET_VELOCITY_LIMIT, and the file header the maker's own slicer writes; qidi: `; CHANGE_LAYER`, `; FEATURE:`, M204; klipper: the flashforge comments and SET_VELOCITY_LIMIT with no maker's header), so its screen and previewers read them; unset = its model's default (model)

arcs.description: the firmware takes arcs (G2/G3) — true or false; or a formula (= ...)

exclude_object.description: the firmware can cancel one object mid-print — true or false; or a formula (= ...)

kind.description: how it changes filament (not yet used)

time.description: the machine's own time for one change, beyond the g-code's moves — a time (s); or a formula (= ...)

pressure_advance.description: pressure advance every tool prints with (Klipper's, in seconds, e.g. "0.035 s") unless the tool or the filament sets its own; none set = the firmware's own, and plymeld writes none — a time (s); or a formula (= ...)

start.description: g-code before the print (plymeld's template variables: nozzle_temperature, first_layer_nozzle_temperature, bed_temperature, first_layer_bed_temperature, layers, max_z, max_layer_z, initial_tool (the tool the print starts with, as T<n>), max_filament_flow (mm3/s), filament_diameter (mm), z_hop (mm, the travel lift: the first filament's retract.z_hop), max_print_height (mm, the machine's build.z))

end.description: g-code after the print (the same variables as the start)

pause.description: g-code that pauses for the user

level.description: g-code that levels the bed (e.g. a bed mesh), run after the start template when a print asks for levelling (a calibration plate does unless --no-level); empty = none known for the machine

layer_change.description: g-code at each layer change (layer_z, layer_number)

pictures.description: the preview pictures its screen reads from the g-code file, as pixel sizes WIDTHxHEIGHT separated by commas (e.g. "96x96, 300x300"): plymeld draws the plate's parts into each and writes it as a PNG in a `; thumbnail begin` comment block near the top of the file; unset or empty = no picture

api.description: the protocol `plymeld printer` speaks to it: flashforge-http = Flashforge's LAN HTTP API (the Creator 5), moonraker = Moonraker's HTTP API on a Klipper machine

host.description: its address on the network (a host name or an IP address)

level.description: `plymeld printer send --print` asks the printer to level the bed before it prints (flashforge-http: levelingBeforePrint); --level / --no-level win over it; unset = false. A printer whose API has no such request (moonraker: levelling there is g-code, gcode.start or gcode.level) refuses it — true or false; or a formula (= ...)

port.description: the API's port; unset = the API's own (8898 for flashforge-http, 7125 for moonraker) — a count; or a formula (= ...)

timeout.description: how long to wait for the printer's answer; unset = 8 s — a time (s); or a formula (= ...)

env.description: the NAME of the environment variable holding one credential the protocol needs (flashforge-http: serial_number and check_code; moonraker: api_key, and for its shell ssh_password or ssh_key_file (the path of a private key), all optional); the value itself never goes in a config file

file.description: a local secrets file (a path, ~/ allowed) holding the credential as a `<name> = "value"` line, a second source beside .env: when both are set and the environment variable has a value, the environment wins; never commit the file

url.description: its camera's URL (a snapshot URL, or an MJPEG stream, as its own web server gives it); unset = the API's own where it names one, else no camera

user.description: the user name for a shell on the printer over SSH (moonraker: `printer loadout` reads the QIDI Box's slots from Klipper's save_variables file through it); unset = no shell, and no loadout from a Moonraker machine

host.description: the address the shell is reached at; unset = connection.host

port.description: the SSH port; unset = 22 — a count; or a formula (= ...)

variables_file.description: the path on the printer of Klipper's save_variables file, where the QIDI Box records its slots; unset = /home/mks/printer_data/config/saved_variables.cfg (a QIDI Q2's layout, as seen on one)

accept_new.description: trust the printer's SSH host key on first use and record it in ~/.ssh/known_hosts (a risk: a machine in between can pose as the printer that first time; see SECURITY.md); unset or false = an unknown or changed host key is refused — true or false; or a formula (= ...)

plate.description: the build plate on its bed now (a calibration plate takes it unless --plate names another) (the key of a plate)

filament.description: the filament in one of its tools (a model's part numbers are the tools' indexes); "" = the tool is empty, which lets a later config file unload a tool an earlier one loads (the key of a filament, or "" for none loaded)

for one nozzle fed by several spools: the filament in a slot (a model's part numbers are the slots); "" = the slot is empty, which lets a later config file unload a slot an earlier one loads (the key of a filament, or "" for none loaded)

tool.description: the tool a slot feeds (default: the machine's only tool) (the key of a tool)

like.description: start from another model's values (a shipped model, or one of yours), every command it accepts included (the key of a model)

name.description: the model's name, as the window and messages show it

profile_name.description: the printer_model another slicer's profile gives this model: the profile importer maps it to this model

dialect.description: the g-code dialect a machine of this model writes unless it sets its own (hardware.machine.<key>.firmware.dialect)

notes.description: notes on the model's description: where its facts come from, what is not known

file.description: the search log's file; empty = search.log in plymeld's state folder; a leading ~/ is your home directory; made with its directories when missing

away.description: how much a face turned squarely away from where the print is looked at from (plan.view_from) counts toward quality's measures (part way: between this and 1), not a seam's (method.quality.visibility.quadrant.*); a placeholder until measured — a multiplier (0.15 or 15%); or a formula (= ...)

front.description: the least-visible seam: how much the sampled viewing directions from the front quadrant count (the 90 degrees around the print's front as seen from plan.view_from; a direction on a quadrant's edge counts the mean of the two); the most-seen open wall reads 1; every direction alike with plan.view_from all_around or above — a multiplier (0.15 or 15%); or a formula (= ...)

right.description: the least-visible seam: how much the sampled viewing directions from the right quadrant count (the 90 degrees around the print's right as seen from plan.view_from; a direction on a quadrant's edge counts the mean of the two); the most-seen open wall reads 1; every direction alike with plan.view_from all_around or above — a multiplier (0.15 or 15%); or a formula (= ...)

azimuths.description: how many viewing directions around the print a seam's point is sampled from, for what hides it nearby (the seam placement and the seam measure); a placeholder — a count; or a formula (= ...)

elevations.description: how many heights each viewing direction is sampled at, evenly from level up to method.quality.visibility.sample.elevation.max (1 = level only); a placeholder — a count; or a formula (= ...)

max.description: the highest viewing direction sampled above level for what hides a seam nearby; a placeholder — a angle (deg); or a formula (= ...)

reach.description: how far from a seam's point a viewing ray is followed for material that hides it (0 = nothing hides it); a placeholder — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

cell.description: the grid each layer's outline is read on when following a viewing ray; a placeholder — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

show_through.description: how deep behind a visible surface a seam still shows through it (a seam whose viewing ray meets only material it leaves within this distance counts 1 - that distance / this); 0 = any material hides a seam; a placeholder — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

depth_power.description: the stair-step measure (surface_step): each face's terrace edges per mm (the sine of its angle to its layer / the layer's height) x each edge's depth to this power (2: an edge half as deep counts a quarter, so thinner layers score better and a face that follows its layer shows few edges); a placeholder until measured — a multiplier (0.15 or 15%); or a formula (= ...)

corner_share.description: the seam measure (seam_scar): a point seam in a corner (a turn of at least plan.technique.corner_seam.corner_angle) as a share of one on a smooth wall; the bundled value measured on a seam plate (plymeld calibrate seams) — a multiplier (0.15 or 15%); or a formula (= ...)

fan_loss.description: the bond between layers lost to a full part fan, against none (the bond factor's fan term, 1 - fan_loss x fan); a placeholder until measured — a multiplier (0.15 or 15%); or a formula (= ...)

temperature_gain.description: the bond between layers gained per 10 C of nozzle above the filament's print temperature (lost below it); a placeholder until measured — a multiplier (0.15 or 15%); or a formula (= ...)

cooling_loss.description: the bond between layers lost when the layer below has cooled for bond.cooling_time or longer (the bond factor's cooling term); a placeholder until measured — a multiplier (0.15 or 15%); or a formula (= ...)

cooling_time.description: the layer time after which the layer below counts as fully cooled for the bond; a placeholder until measured — a time (s); or a formula (= ...)

enough_area.description: a weakest bond between layers this large (after the bond factor) is strong enough: bond.strength gains nothing above it; a placeholder until measured — a area (mm2); or a formula (= ...)

tolerance.description: outline simplification — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

close_gaps.description: gaps narrower than twice this are closed — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

technique.description: the surface technique locked on the flat tops: ironing = smooth, the nozzle passed over them again laying almost no plastic (plan.technique.ironing); as_laid = as the volume technique lays them. Unset = as laid

the surface technique locked on the sloped tops: z_antialiasing = the stair-steps removed: in flat layers, where the model's top lies within a layer, its lines are lowered onto the top with less plastic (never thinner than the tool's thinnest layer, hardware.tool.<key>.layer.height.min), and the layer reaches out to where the top is that far above its bottom; curved and lifted layers follow their own surfaces; as_laid = as laid. Unset = as laid (Z anti-aliasing until a print decides it)
the surface technique locked on the walls: fuzzy_skin = rough, jittered in and out on the walls plan.technique.fuzzy_skin.where names; as_laid = as laid. Unset = as laid

the surface technique locked on the undersides over air: wave_overhang = each flat layer's bottom over air that hangs off one side grown outward from the supported material beside it, bead by bead, each bead laid against the one before at plan.technique.wave_overhang's spacing, flow, and speed (a span, every bridge line landing on what is printed at both ends, stays a bridge; an area with support under it is the support's; what no front reaches is bridged); as_laid = bridged, as before. Bundled: wave_overhang (wave overhang, support, or nothing for an underside hanging off one side; never bridged)

from.description: where the underside surface technique starts: only layers whose top is above this height (from the object's bottom, as printed) get it; unset = from the bottom — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

to.description: where the underside surface technique ends: only layers whose bottom is below this height (from the object's bottom, as printed) get it; unset = to the top — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

seam.description: the seam style locked for the wall loops: scarf_seam = scarf seams on the outer walls above the first layer that plan.technique.scarf_seam.where names (never on a fuzzed wall, nor a loop Z anti-aliasing lowers), placed and its other loops seamed as its plain_style; corner_seam = every loop starts at a corner when it has one (inside corners first), each layer's seam nearest the one below (with none below: the sharpest corner, else the back-most point); back_seam = every loop starts at its back-most point; least_visible_seam = every loop starts at the held-up point the seam measure counts least (its visibility, turned away from plan.view_from's viewer or an underside, times method.quality.seam.corner_share in a corner), ties to the point the viewer sees least first (a turned-away face before a front corner), then to a corner, then to the seam below, then the back. Either way, a point on an edge of the layer that hangs over the layer below (where the overhang slow-down starts) only when the loop has no other. Unset = decided per object by the job's weights (seam_scar against the scarf's extra pass in time)

at.description: pause before the first layer whose top is at or above this height — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

enabled.description: the support switch, a lock: true = tree support under every face too steep to hold itself up; false = never (and a locked spot, plan.support.locked, is then refused); unset = the search decides per overhang (coordination phase 3), weighing each region's scars and plastic against the droop without it, with the locked spots always supported — true or false; or a formula (= ...)
