slot.description: the slot that prints support interface (0 = whichever is loaded) — a count; or a formula (= ...)

value.description: the gap between support's top and the object it holds up, rounded to whole layers; unset = one layer, at least gap.top.min — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

min.description: the least gap between support's top and the object when gap.top.value is unset: one layer, or as many as reach this (0.2 mm: 3 layers at 0.08 mm) — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

bottom.description: the gap between support standing on the model and the model's top under it; the support's lowest interface.bottom_layers above the gap are bottom interface, as on the bed; unset = one layer (the layer on the model's top left out); 0 = laid onto it — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

side.description: the gap beside the object, between support and the object's walls; unset = plymeld's rule, one support line — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

width.description: the narrowest column of support laid, so the narrowest overhang that gets support: an overhang is kept only where the overhang within this height above and below it, taken together, is at least this wide (a sloped face is a stack of thin strips, judged as a stack); what is narrower is a speck nothing could stand under and gets no support, a locked spot excepted; unset = plymeld's rule, a tree tip (two support lines) — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

spacing.description: INHERITED: gap between support lines — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

from_bed_only.description: INHERITED: only support standing on the bed — true or false; or a formula (= ...)

width.description: INHERITED: support line width — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

angle.description: INHERITED: support line direction — a angle (deg); or a formula (= ...)

slot.description: the slot that prints support (0 = whichever is loaded) — a count; or a formula (= ...)

branch_diameter.description: INHERITED: largest branch diameter — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

widening.description: INHERITED: how fast a branch widens going down — a angle (deg); or a formula (= ...)

tip_spacing.description: INHERITED: spacing of the tips under an overhang — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

min.description: a planned insert: a socket the print pauses at so an object is placed in it, the layer over it printed onto the object's top (no bridge, no support in the socket); the box's least corner, in the model's own coordinates; the pose must be locked (plan.pose = "as-given" or plan.object.<key>.pose.turn) and keep the socket opening upward — a point, x y z and a unit ("10 20 5 mm"); or an array of 3 numbers (mm)

max.description: the insert's box's greatest corner (above min on every axis), in the model's own coordinates — a point, x y z and a unit ("10 20 5 mm"); or an array of 3 numbers (mm)

top.description: the insert's top once placed, in the model's own z (unset: the box's top, max's z): the pause comes before the first layer whose bottom is at or above it, and that layer's bottom over the socket is laid onto the insert — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

pose.description: how each object sits: decided, or the model's own orientation

printing.description: objects printed together or one after another

order.description: the order objects printed one at a time (plan.objects.printing = one_at_a_time) go in: shortest_first (unset) = the shortest first; as_given = the order the objects are given (the models in the order loaded); the head's reach and the nozzle-to-rod height are checked against the objects already printed either way

bridge_order.description: objects printed together: by_height (unset) = every object's layers merged by height; hot_to_cold = every object's layers below its lifted bridge first (merged by height, at the print temperature), then the lifted bridges one bridge temperature at a time, hottest first (objects by plan.technique.bridge.temperature, unset = the print temperature), the head lifted clear of everything printed between groups: one temperature change per group, each a cooling; one_at_a_time = the layers below every lifted bridge first, then each object's bridge whole, one object after another from +X to -X, a fixed order that suits a head reaching least towards +X (it then never passes over a finished bridge); the head's reach is not read yet, and the layout must leave room

additionalProperties.description: fingerprint of an object's geometry when the plan was made
fingerprint of one section (hardware, model, job, method) of the config the plan was made from

top_order.description: the order of a curved band's top surface lines: one_way (unset) = one sweep across the surface, as any top, so on one side of a peak each new line goes down beside the one before, below it; uphill = the lines split where the surface is highest, each side laid from its lowest line up to it, so each new line goes down beside the one before on its low side (plate 8's solid arch came out rough on the half its top was swept down)

height.description: flat layers: the layer height where they keep one height (and of the flat layers under a curved band or holding up a lifted bridge); decided by the search over the tool's thinnest to thickest layer unless set in a config (the bundled value is only the stand-in other values are worked out from) — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

max.description: flat layers following the surfaces: the deepest stair-step a layer may leave (unset: the layer height) — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

height_ratio.description: the transition between layer heights: no layer (after the first) more than this much thicker than the one below it, and the layers before a band whose layers start thinner stepping down by about this much each ("1.5": a 0.08 mm band meets a 0.28 mm one through 0.12, 0.18, 0.27); "0" = no limit, a jump at the band's boundary — a multiplier (0.15 or 15%); or a formula (= ...)

layers.description: the hidden core in thicker layers: every this many layers, the sparse infill those layers share is laid once, on the last of them, the layers' height thick (within the tool's thickest layer); each layer's sparse infill outside what the group shares is laid on its own layer. "1" = every layer its own (off). Bundled: as many layers as fit the tool's thickest layer — a count; or a formula (= ...)

heights.description: how flat layers set their heights: one = one layer height for the whole object; follow = every layer as thick as the surfaces it crosses allow (needs the tool's thinnest and thickest layer, and no fuzzy skin); derive (or unset) = the search weighs both, and the bands flat layers' survey proposes (following the surfaces there, one height elsewhere)

fan.description: bond-first cooling's part fan for the object's lines; bundled half the filament's cooling.fan, a placeholder — a multiplier (0.15 or 15%); or a formula (= ...)

min.description: bond-first cooling's minimum layer time; bundled half the filament's, a placeholder — a time (s); or a formula (= ...)

temperature.description: bond-first cooling's nozzle temperature after the first layer, capped at the filament's temperature.max where set; bundled the filament's print temperature + 10 C, a placeholder — a temperature (C); or a formula (= ...)

ramp_speeds.description: an ARCHED lifted bridge's speeds over air in its layers after its first: its first layer's segments over the hollow at bridge.print.speed, the next layers' at these speeds in turn, in mm/s separated by commas (e.g. "6, 8, 12, 24 mm/s"), then each bridge.ramp_growth times the last, every one capped at the bridge speed (plan.mechanism.motion.bridge.speed), the ramp ending with the first that reaches it; the usual speeds after. Every segment over what holds the bridge up at the usual speeds throughout. Empty with ramp_growth "1" = no ramp: the usual speeds from the second layer. After a wave overhang's layer (its beads at wave_overhang.speed), the layers over the beads take the bridge's whole sequence: bridge.print.speed, then these, then the growth

ramp_growth.description: after bridge.ramp_speeds, each layer's speed over air of an ARCHED lifted bridge this many times the last, up to the bridge speed; "1" or less = no growth: the usual speeds after the listed ones — a multiplier (0.15 or 15%); or a formula (= ...)

temperature.description: the nozzle temperature of an ARCHED lifted bridge's own layers (its first layer arching above or below straight between its supports by more than half a layer: an arch, a sag; not a flat, ramp, or valley bridge), waited for before them; the rest of the object (what holds the bridge up) at its print temperature, waited for again after; over plan.mechanism.temperature.print and the filament's. Unset: the print temperature — a temperature (C); or a formula (= ...)

speed.description: an ARCHED lifted bridge's first layer, where it is over air (tacks too), at this speed, its next layers stepping up to the bridge speed as bridge.ramp_speeds and ramp_growth say; what lies over the bridge's supports at the usual speeds: no slow-down for layer time, no floor, no overhang grading on the slow segments (the melt cap still applies: it only lowers a speed when the filament cannot melt fast enough). Unset: the usual speeds — a speed (mm/s); or a formula (= ...)

every head move that extrudes nothing in an ARCHED lifted bridge's layers (travels, lifts, the drops into tacks) at most this fast; not retractions and their restores, which keep the filament's speeds. Unset: the usual speeds — a speed (mm/s); or a formula (= ...)

fill_angles.description: the direction of a lifted bridge's fill from its first layer up (its bottom, solid, sparse, and top fill): span (unset) = at its span's direction (as its first layer's bridge lines take it between its anchors) and at right angles to it, layer by layer, counted from its top so its top layer runs along the span, foot to foot; a grid's or cubic's sparse families from the span; object = the object's own fill directions (plan.layer.infill.angle, turned 90 deg layer by layer). With fill_along = true every fill but the top runs along the span either way

fill_along.description: a lifted bridge's layers all along its bridge: from its first layer up, every fill (bottom, solid) at the angle its first layer's bridge lines take; its top surface keeps its usual angle ("Allow for non-parallel motion on the top/finishing layers") — true or false; or a formula (= ...)

height.description: a lifted bridge's own layer height, for an object with several lifted bridges (each printed after the layer it rests on): what holds them up keeps the object's layer height (the double helix's wall at 0.1 mm, its arches at 0.2). Unset: the object's layer height. A lone lifted bridge shares the object's layers: a different value is refused — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

top_layer.description: an ARCHED lifted bridge's top layer (its last, when it has more than one): normal = at the usual speeds and the print temperature (waited for), ironing with it; bridge = at the bridge's own speeds and temperature, as its other layers

first_layer.description: a lifted bridge's first layer: lines (unset) = bridge lines from support to support; wave_overhang = wave beads (plan.technique.wave_overhang's spacing, overlap, line area, and speed) grown from every support at once over the whole span, each bead climbing from its support once lifted onto an arch, one support's side whole and then the other's, meeting where they are equally far from both (the peak of a symmetric arch); its layers above as the bridge's others

sides.description: the order of a waved first layer's sides (plan.technique.bridge.first_layer = wave_overhang): one_then_other (unset) = one support's side whole, then the other's; alternate = front by front, each front's beads on one side and then on the other, so neither side reaches out alone while the other is laid (every bead still climbs from its own support, and each side's edge beads come last); one_support = the fronts grow from one support only (the first in order of x then y) across the whole span, climbing to the peak and descending to the other support

order.description: when a waved first layer's edge pieces (its beads along the span's edges, each from its support up to the middle) are laid: with_each_side (unset) = after that side's beads across; last = after every bead across on both sides (with wave.sides = alternate they come last either way)

enabled.description: whether a waved first layer's edge pieces are laid at all: false = the beads across end at the span's edges; unset = laid — true or false; or a formula (= ...)

direction.description: which edge a waved first layer's beads across the span start from: mirrored (unset) = as grown, each side's beads from one edge, the two sides from opposite edges; matched = every bead from the same edge of the span; zigzag = as matched, every other front's beads from the other edge, so the starts and ends spread over both edges

crossing.description: how the head travels between a waved first layer's beads across the span: over (unset) = straight, above the bridge; beside = between the sides (wave.sides = alternate), out past the span's edge by wave.crossing_clearance, along it, and back in, so ooze on the way does not land on the bridge; away = after every bead across the span, out along the bead's own direction to wave.away.distance from the object (its outline seen from above, as a box), round the object at that distance the shorter way, and in to the next bead's start along that bead's direction, so the hot head is far from the beads between them; a wait (wave.wait, wave.wait_zones) is spent at the far point. The way round is not checked against the other objects on the plate: lay them out clear of it

distance.description: how far from the object the head goes after each bead with wave.crossing = away; unset there is an error — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

wait_zones.description: waits after the beads across the span that vary along it, over wave.wait: zones of the span from the first support (in order of x then y) to the second, in percent, each with its wait, separated by commas (e.g. "0-40%: 5 s, 40-60%: 10 s, 60-100%: 0 s"); a bead takes the wait of the zone its middle lies in, spent before the next bead (at the far point with wave.crossing = away, else lifted over the next bead's start); the last bead waits none. Unset = wave.wait after every bead

zones.description: a waved first layer's lines across the span laid a second time over it, after the whole layer, where zones of the span say (unset = none): zones from the first support (in order of x then y) to the second, in percent of the gap between them, each with how far above the first pass its lines are laid and their plastic as a share of the first pass's, separated by commas (e.g. "25-40%: 0.1 mm 50%, 40-60%: 0 mm 100%, 60-75%: 0.1 mm 50%"); a line belongs to the zone its middle lies in, and runs the other way to the line under it; the lines from the zones' outer ends inward, the two sides in turn, a line at the middle last; no edge pieces; at wave.second_pass.speed, each travel straight, lifted, and each line's start reached straight down from wave.second_pass.approach above it

speed.description: the speed of a waved first layer's second pass (wave.second_pass.zones); unset there is an error — a speed (mm/s); or a formula (= ...)

approach.description: how far above each line's start of a waved first layer's second pass the head comes straight down from (wave.second_pass.zones); unset there is an error — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

enabled.description: Xs over a waved first layer, laid after the whole layer (its edge pieces too): the span in sections of wave.x_length from each support, the one at the middle taking what is left of both sides; each X corner to corner between its section's first and last lines across the span, its ends wave.x_layer.inset in from the span's edges, wave.x_layer.raise above the layer at wave.x_layer.share of its lines' plastic; the two sides in turn from the supports to the middle, the middle X last; at wave.x_layer.speed. Needs a span between two supports and wave.spacing = even; unset = none — true or false; or a formula (= ...)

raise.description: how far above a waved first layer's top its Xs are laid (wave.x_layer.enabled; the X's line its own height under that); unset there is an error — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

share.description: the Xs' plastic per mm as a share of the waved first layer's lines' (wave.x_layer.enabled); unset there is an error — a multiplier (0.15 or 15%); or a formula (= ...)

inset.description: how far in from the span's edges each X's ends stop (wave.x_layer.enabled); unset there is an error — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

middle.description: when the X over the middle of a waved first layer's Xs is laid (wave.x_layer.enabled): last (unset) = after the sides' Xs; first = before them, the sides' then from the supports inward as before

speed.description: the speed of the Xs over a waved first layer (wave.x_layer.enabled); unset there is an error — a speed (mm/s); or a formula (= ...)

enabled.description: a full layer of lines along the span over a waved first layer, laid after it (and after its Xs, wave.x_layer): from support to support over the gap, at the solid fill's width and spacing (plan.layer.solid.line.width) across the gap's width, each the other way to the one before, wave.span_layer.raise above the waved layer's top, at wave.span_layer.speed and the solid fill's plastic. Needs a span between two supports and wave.spacing = even; unset = none — true or false; or a formula (= ...)

raise.description: how far above a waved first layer's top its layer of lines along the span is laid (wave.span_layer.enabled; the line's own height under that), at most two layers; unset there is an error — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

speed.description: the speed of the layer of lines along the span over a waved first layer (wave.span_layer.enabled); unset there is an error — a speed (mm/s); or a formula (= ...)

spacing.description: how a waved first layer's lines are spaced along the span: as_grown (unset) = each front wave_overhang.spacing on from the last, as measured from above, the two sides' last lines left with whatever space remains between them; even = the span from each support's first line to the other's divided into an even number of equal steps, as near wave_overhang.spacing as can be, measured along the bridge's surface (an arch's slopes as well as its top), so the lines lie equally far apart all along it and there is an odd number of them: each side's from its support, and one in the middle, laid after both sides' lines (with wave.line.direction = zigzag running the other way to both sides' last lines); each line straight across the span between its edges. Needs a span between two supports, wave.layers = 1, wave.start = whole and wave.front = straight; with wave.sides = one_support it does not apply

crossing_clearance.description: how far past the span's edge the head goes on a crossing beside the bridge (wave.crossing = beside); plymeld's bundled value is a placeholder — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

retract.description: the retraction before each travel between a waved first layer's beads, over the filament's retract.length (unset = the filament's) — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

wipe.description: whether the head wipes along the bead it has just laid while retracting before each travel between a waved first layer's beads, over the filament's retract.wipe.enabled (unset = the filament's); the wipe's distance, speed, and share as the filament's — true or false; or a formula (= ...)

wait.description: a wait before each bead of a waved first layer but its first, the head lifted over the bead's start (unset = none): more time for the bead before to cool — a time (s); or a formula (= ...)

layers.description: how many of a lifted bridge's first layers are laid as waves (plan.technique.bridge.first_layer = wave_overhang): 1 (unset) = the first; 2 = the first two together, the second's beads the first's fronts one layer up, laid one front behind the first's on each side in turn, so the second layer lands only where the first already reaches one front further out (needs wave.sides = alternate)

second_layer.description: with two waved layers (wave.layers = 2), the second: full (unset) = every front, laid one front behind the first's; x = only an X over each section of the first layer (wave.x_length along the span), its two diagonals corner to corner from the section's first front's ends to its last front's, laid on each side as soon as the first layer covers its whole section; the sections run from each support, and the one at the middle, over where the sides meet, takes what is left of both sides (at least one section): the X's triangles stay open, and the rest of that layer over the gap is left to them but for the strip's edges, laid as on a full second layer (needs two supports, each front one line across)

x_length.description: how far along the span each X of a waved second layer reaches (wave.second_layer = x), rounded to whole fronts (wave_overhang.spacing apart; at least two); unset with wave.second_layer = x is an error — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

start.description: the region a waved first layer lays first, as it lays a whole span (wave.sides, wave.line.direction, wave.crossing as set), before the rest of the span is filled with waves grown from the supports and from what was laid, front by front: whole (unset) = the whole span, nothing after; edge_strips = a strip wave.strip.width wide along each edge of the span, support to support; triangles = from each support a triangle as wide as the span there, narrowing to a point at the middle of one edge, the two meeting there; opposite_triangles = as triangles, the second support's point on the other edge. Every value but whole needs two supports and wave.layers = 1; with wave.sides = one_support it does not apply (the whole span is laid from the one support)

width.description: each edge strip's width with wave.start = edge_strips; unset there is an error — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

front.description: the shape of a waved first layer's fronts across the span: straight (unset) = as they grow from the supports; chevron = fronts shaped as chevrons, one part leading the rest by wave.chevron.lead (wave.chevron.leading: the edges, unset, or the middle), their lines along the fronts or across (wave.chevron.lines) (needs two supports, wave.layers = 1 and wave.start = whole; with wave.sides = one_support it does not apply)

lead.description: how far a chevron front's leading part (wave.chevron.leading) leads the rest along the span (wave.front = chevron); unset = half the span, so with the edges leading the supports' triangles meet at the middle of the edges, and with the middle leading at the center point: the angle follows the bridge's width and span — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

leading.description: which part of a chevron front leads (wave.front = chevron): edges (unset) = the edges, by wave.chevron.lead: from each support two triangles along the edges, the diamond between them last, closing on the center point; middle = the middle: from each support a triangle out of the support's middle, its tip leading, the two tips meeting at the center point first; then the regions along the edges, closing at the middle of each edge last

lines.description: how a chevron's lines run (wave.front = chevron): along_fronts (unset) = along each front, diagonal, each front a line (or a ring where the fronts close in); across = every line parallel to the support's edge, as on a straight-front waved bridge, each row from a support laid in at most three pieces: first the part the leading region reaches (the middle piece with wave.chevron.leading = middle, else the two edge pieces), row by row from each support outward, then the rest of each row the same way, each piece from the leading region out

after_supported.description: whether a waved first layer's lines come after what that layer lays on the supports (the strip over them): true = its first lines attach to that strip's edge at their own height as well as to the supports' top; unset = before it, the first lines resting on the supports' edge by wave_overhang.overlap alone (with wave.layers = 2 or wave.front = chevron they come after it either way) — true or false; or a formula (= ...)

layers.description: how many of a lifted bridge's layers after its first are tacked to it (0: none): on each, before the layer, a short line where its first layer's bridge lines arch furthest from straight, laid at the height the layer would have over a first layer pulled straight between its ends, then rising back to the layer — a count; or a formula (= ...)

length.description: how long each tack runs at its low height, along the bridge line — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

rise.description: how far along the line the tack rises back to the layer's height — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

spacing.description: how far apart the tacked bridge lines lie across the bridge: its two outermost first, then lines this far apart — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

how far each front of a wave overhang lies from the last: the beads' center spacing, under a line width so each bead leans on the one before (the sources: about 0.35 mm for a 0.4 mm nozzle) — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

overlap.description: how far the first bead reaches back over the supported material it starts from — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

min.description: a neck of the overhang narrower than this is not spanned: what lies beyond it is bridged — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)
growth stops when a front adds less than this — a area (mm2); or a formula (= ...)

area.description: the plastic per mm of a wave bead, as the bead's cross-section: laid in the air with nothing to squash it against, the layer height does not set it (the sources: 0.16 mm² for a 0.4 mm nozzle) — a area (mm2); or a formula (= ...)

speed.description: every wave bead at this speed (the sources: about 2 mm/s; over about 5 the bead no longer holds) — a speed (mm/s); or a formula (= ...)

spacing.description: gap between ironing lines — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

flow.description: ironing flow, a share of a full line — a multiplier (0.15 or 15%); or a formula (= ...)

inset.description: keep this far inside the edge — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

angle.description: ironing direction — a angle (deg); or a formula (= ...)

speed.description: ironing speed — a speed (mm/s); or a formula (= ...)

where.description: which walls fuzzy skin takes: external = the outside outlines, all = with the holes, allwalls = every wall

thickness.description: how far points move, ± — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

point_distance.description: average spacing of the points — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

first_layer.description: fuzz the first layer too — true or false; or a formula (= ...)

where.description: which outer walls get a scarf seam: smooth = only loops whose seam does not land on a corner (with the plain style corner_seam, the loops with no corner; with back_seam, most loops), all = every outer wall. A scarf seam starts the loop thin and low, rising to the layer over scarf_seam.length, and ends re-printing that stretch thinning to nothing (the two wedges make one layer)

length.description: how long a scarf seam's ramp is (at most half the loop; a loop too short for a ramp of two line widths gets none) — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

start.description: a scarf ramp's starting thickness, as a share of the layer (0 starts from nothing, the nozzle on the layer below) — a multiplier (0.15 or 15%); or a formula (= ...)

plain_style.description: the plain seam style beside scarf seams: a scarf seam starts where it would start the loop, and it seams every loop the scarf seams do not take

corner_angle.description: the smallest turn of a wall loop (measured across two line widths each side) that counts as a corner for its seam (also for scarf seams' where = smooth) — a angle (deg); or a formula (= ...)

thickness.description: INHERITED: wall thickness (the number of wall lines follows from the line width) — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

style.description: INHERITED: wall lines of one width, or variable width in thin areas

width.description: INHERITED: outer wall line width — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)
INHERITED: inner wall line width — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

inner_first.description: INHERITED: inner walls before the outer one — true or false; or a formula (= ...)

thickness.description: INHERITED: solid thickness under a top — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

pattern.description: INHERITED: top surface pattern (concentric-outside-in: loops following the outline, each the one outside it moved in; concentric-inside-out: round rings around the surface's middle, arcs where a full circle does not fit)

under_parts.description: a top surface that is mostly exposed runs under the other parts standing on it: its pattern unbroken, as if nothing stood there — true or false; or a formula (= ...)

width.description: INHERITED: top surface line width — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

thickness.description: INHERITED: solid thickness over a bottom — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

density.description: INHERITED: share of the interior filled — a multiplier (0.15 or 15%); or a formula (= ...)

pattern.description: INHERITED: the interior's pattern (gyroid: curves, the gyroid surface's cross-section; the interior angle does not apply to it)

width.description: INHERITED: interior line width — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

angle.description: INHERITED: interior line direction — a angle (deg); or a formula (= ...)

chord_tolerance.description: INHERITED: how far a curved interior line (the gyroid's) may stray from the true curve between two of its vertices: the traced curve is simplified to it before it is laid. Unset (bundled) = laid as traced, where the arc fitter turns its runs into arcs; set it for a printer without arcs (fewer, longer straight segments). With arcs on, simplifying first is slower: the simplified curve no longer fits as arcs (a 9 h print's gyroid 843,112 arcs -> 15,215, predicted 14 min slower). Not the outline tolerance (method.slicing.tolerance) — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

wall_overlap.description: how far an interior line's end reaches into the walls past bead contact, as a share of its width (a line end touches a wall only with its rounded cap) — a multiplier (0.15 or 15%); or a formula (= ...)

cells.description: a sparse piece narrower than this many cells of its pattern is narrow (default 1) — a multiplier (0.15 or 15%); or a formula (= ...)

fill.description: what a narrow sparse piece gets: one loop (default) or solid

width.description: INHERITED: internal solid line width — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

flow.description: INHERITED: bridge extrusion multiplier — a multiplier (0.15 or 15%); or a formula (= ...)

speed.description: speed of visible lines: outer walls, top and bottom surfaces; a value in a config of yours wins over the machine's (hardware.machine.<key>.motion.visible.speed, from its motion plate); plymeld's bundled value is only the stand-in for a machine that sets none (until decided from the quality weight) — a speed (mm/s); or a formula (= ...)

acceleration.description: acceleration of visible lines; the rest print at the machine's printing acceleration; a value in a config of yours wins over the machine's (hardware.machine.<key>.motion.visible.acceleration); plymeld's bundled value is only the stand-in — a accel (mm/s2); or a formula (= ...)

speed.description: speed of everything on the first layer (adhesion): a value in a config locks it over the filament's first-layer window (hardware.filament.<key>.first_layer.window.<plate>), its motion.first_layer.speed, and the machine's (hardware.machine.<key>.motion.first_layer.speed); plymeld's bundled value is only the stand-in for a machine and filament that set none — a speed (mm/s); or a formula (= ...)
bridge speed; a wall line slows toward it as more of it hangs over air — a speed (mm/s); or a formula (= ...)

margin.description: avoid_crossing: how far outside an island's outer wall a detour runs (beyond the wall's center line plus half its width); bundled 1 mm, a placeholder — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

max.description: avoid_crossing: a detour longer than this many times the straight travel plus detour.extra.max is not taken (the straight travel with its lift is); bundled 2, a placeholder — a multiplier (0.15 or 15%); or a formula (= ...)
avoid_crossing: the length added to detour.ratio.max times the straight travel that a detour may still have; bundled 20 mm, a placeholder — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

avoid_crossing: a travel to or from an outer-wall speck routed along the wall it lines (where combing finds no way inside) is not taken when longer than this many times the straight travel plus detour.speck.extra.max; bundled 5 — a multiplier (0.15 or 15%); or a formula (= ...)
avoid_crossing: the length added to detour.speck.ratio.max times the straight travel that a route along the wall to or from a speck may still have; bundled 50 mm — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

inset.description: avoid_crossing: how far inside an island's outer wall (its center line) a travel within the island runs; unset = the widest outer wall's line width on the layer. Where no route stays this far inside (material thinner than two insets), a half, a quarter, and an eighth of it are tried, so the route runs down the material's middle — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

avoid_crossing.description: travels go around the layer's other islands rather than straight over them (a string a travel draws then lies over nothing): every closed outer wall of the layer is an island, its convex hull detour.margin outside the wall; and a travel within one island stays inside it, detour.inset inside its outer walls (never out over an edge or across a notch in its outline; a travel to an outer-wall speck just past the walls, a line kept because it lines the outline, hops out to it only at the speck; where no route inside reaches a speck, the travel runs along the outer wall it lines, retracting as usual, within detour.speck.ratio.max and detour.speck.extra.max); an island the travel leaves or enters cannot be avoided; a detour or route longer than detour.ratio.max times the straight travel plus detour.extra.max is not taken — true or false; or a formula (= ...)

no_retract_in_island.description: no retraction and no lift for a travel whose straight path stays inside the island being printed (the piece of the layer it is on), crosses no wall line already laid on the layer nor any outer wall of the layer, and neither leaves nor enters a top surface or ironing (above the first layer); a travel that leaves the island, crosses a gap or a wall retracts and lifts as usual. Unset = decided per object by the plan on its planned layers, by the job's weights (the strings those travels risk against the restarts and the time of retracting them; plan and slice say which, `plan -o` writes it); true = on (a helix island's runs each retracted, lifted, and restored for 1-2 mm moves inside it); false = every travel over retract.travel.min retracts and lifts, except those plymeld keeps hidden inside the infill and the travel into an outer-wall speck (a wall line shorter than two of its widths) that passes these tests or is reached from its own outer wall in its island, then lifted over that wall but not retracted (a restart for a dot left a blob) — true or false; or a formula (= ...)

print.description: the nozzle temperature after the first layer, over the filament's temperature.print; set on an object or part (plan.object.<key>.mechanism.temperature.print) for that one only — a temperature (C); or a formula (= ...)

first_layer.description: the nozzle temperature on the first layer, over the filament's temperature.first_layer (not changed by temperature.print) — a temperature (C); or a formula (= ...)

fan.description: the part fan for an object's or part's lines from its fan-on layer, over the filament's cooling.fan; set on an object or part (plan.object.<key>.mechanism.cooling.fan) for that one only. Its overhang lines keep the filament's overhang.fan — a multiplier (0.15 or 15%); or a formula (= ...)

min.description: an object's or part's minimum layer time, over the filament's cooling.layer.time.min; set on an object or part for that one only — a time (s); or a formula (= ...)

style.description: how a layer is slowed to its minimum layer time: hidden_first = the hidden lines first (inner walls, infill, support), each down to the minimum speed, the visible lines (outer walls, top and bottom surfaces) only for what they cannot give; even = every line by one factor

enabled.description: a layer still short of its minimum layer time with every line at the minimum speed: true = the head waits out the rest, retracted, as dwell.style says; false = printed as it is — true or false; or a formula (= ...)

style.description: how the head waits: lift = straight up from where the layer ended, dwell.lift (within the machine's height), so it keeps its distance from the part and any ooze stays put; park = beside the layer, lifted clear, the nozzle where the head's edge just clears the layer's printed area on the nearest side within the bed (from hardware.tool.<key>.head.size and head.nozzle.x / head.nozzle.y; without them no wait, said in a comment)

lift.description: how far the head rises for a lift dwell (dwell.style = lift) — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

overhang_fan.description: the part fan for an object's or part's lines over air (overhangs, bridges), over the filament's overhang.fan; set on an object or part for that one only. Over air the fan is the larger of this and cooling.fan — a multiplier (0.15 or 15%); or a formula (= ...)

height.description: INHERITED: first layer height; a value in a config locks it over the filament's first-layer window (hardware.filament.<key>.first_layer.window.<plate>); plymeld's bundled value is the stand-in without one — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

width.description: INHERITED: first layer line width — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

enabled.description: INHERITED: a brim around the first layer — true or false; or a formula (= ...)

where.description: INHERITED: where the brim goes: outer = around the outside of the first layer

width.description: INHERITED: brim width — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

gap.description: INHERITED: gap between brim and object — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

enabled.description: a separate prime line before the first layer. Unset: on when prime.line is set, else off with a prime tower and on otherwise — true or false; or a formula (= ...)

line.description: where the prime line lies: near = alongside the first object, prime.gap from it; tab = the same on a peel tab, a partial brim joining it to the print (alongside the brim's outer edge when there is a brim). Unset: tab (near the model, with a brim, by default)

length.description: the prime line's length — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

gap.description: how far the prime line lies from the print (from the brim's outer edge on a tab) — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

enabled.description: INHERITED: purge into a tower — true or false; or a formula (= ...)

layout.description: INHERITED: visit the tower only on layers with a change, or every layer

x.description: INHERITED: tower position, X — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

y.description: INHERITED: tower position, Y — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

into.description: where the new filament's purge goes after a tool change: tower = all of it into the tower; infill = first into that filament's own sparse infill on the layer (printed right after the change, the dirtiest plastic hidden), the tower taking what is left; infill_and_object = its sparse infill, then its hidden solid infill, then the tower. Per object or part (plan.object.<key>.mechanism.purge.into) where a light part must not take a dark purge behind thin walls

bond_cooling.description: bond-first cooling for an object (plan.object.<key>.bond_cooling) or every object: on = its lines at plan.technique.bond_cooling's fan, minimum layer time, and nozzle temperature (the bond between layers before the filament's cooling); off = the filament's cooling. Unset = weighed per object by the job's weights: the bond (bond.strength, strength) against the cooling it gives up (cooling_shortfall, quality); only an object whose weakest bond is under method.strength.bond.enough_area gains anything, so the rest keep the filament's cooling

view_from.description: where the finished print is looked at from, for quality's measures (the visibility map): all_around = no face counts as turned away; front, back, left, right, above = the model's own sides as given (front is its small-y side, toward the printer's door when it prints as given), turned with whatever pose the plan gives it. A face turned away from the viewer counts method.quality.visibility.away by how squarely it faces away; a seam placed least_visible goes where its viewing directions, weighed by the quadrant they look from (method.quality.visibility.quadrant.*), see it least. Per object: plan.object.<key>.view_from

object.description: per-object values, by object key (`name`, `name#2` ...); they win over the general ones

technique.description: the surface technique locked on the flat tops: ironing = smooth, the nozzle passed over them again laying almost no plastic (plan.technique.ironing); as_laid = as the volume technique lays them. Unset = as laid

the surface technique locked on the sloped tops: z_antialiasing = the stair-steps removed: in flat layers, where the model's top lies within a layer, its lines are lowered onto the top with less plastic (never thinner than the tool's thinnest layer, hardware.tool.<key>.layer.height.min), and the layer reaches out to where the top is that far above its bottom; curved and lifted layers follow their own surfaces; as_laid = as laid. Unset = as laid (Z anti-aliasing until a print decides it)
the surface technique locked on the walls: fuzzy_skin = rough, jittered in and out on the walls plan.technique.fuzzy_skin.where names; as_laid = as laid. Unset = as laid

the surface technique locked on the undersides over air: wave_overhang = each flat layer's bottom over air that hangs off one side grown outward from the supported material beside it, bead by bead, each bead laid against the one before at plan.technique.wave_overhang's spacing, flow, and speed (a span, every bridge line landing on what is printed at both ends, stays a bridge; an area with support under it is the support's; what no front reaches is bridged); as_laid = bridged, as before. Bundled: wave_overhang (wave overhang, support, or nothing for an underside hanging off one side; never bridged)

from.description: where the underside surface technique starts: only layers whose top is above this height (from the object's bottom, as printed) get it; unset = from the bottom — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

to.description: where the underside surface technique ends: only layers whose bottom is below this height (from the object's bottom, as printed) get it; unset = to the top — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

seam.description: the seam style locked for the wall loops: scarf_seam = scarf seams on the outer walls above the first layer that plan.technique.scarf_seam.where names (never on a fuzzed wall, nor a loop Z anti-aliasing lowers), placed and its other loops seamed as its plain_style; corner_seam = every loop starts at a corner when it has one (inside corners first), each layer's seam nearest the one below (with none below: the sharpest corner, else the back-most point); back_seam = every loop starts at its back-most point; least_visible_seam = every loop starts at the held-up point the seam measure counts least (its visibility, turned away from plan.view_from's viewer or an underside, times method.quality.seam.corner_share in a corner), ties to the point the viewer sees least first (a turned-away face before a front corner), then to a corner, then to the seam below, then the back. Either way, a point on an edge of the layer that hangs over the layer below (where the overhang slow-down starts) only when the loop has no other. Unset = decided per object by the job's weights (seam_scar against the scarf's extra pass in time)

min.description: a spot support is locked on (a requirement the search never weighs away: every downward face in the box gets support, whether or not it needs it; plymeld refuses when nothing in the box can be supported): the box's least corner, in the model's own coordinates as its file gives them — a point, x y z and a unit ("10 20 5 mm"); or an array of 3 numbers (mm)

max.description: the locked spot's greatest corner (above min on every axis), in the model's own coordinates — a point, x y z and a unit ("10 20 5 mm"); or an array of 3 numbers (mm)

enabled.description: the support switch, a lock: true = tree support under every face too steep to hold itself up; false = never (and a locked spot, plan.support.locked, is then refused); unset = the search decides per overhang (coordination phase 3), weighing each region's scars and plastic against the droop without it, with the locked spots always supported — true or false; or a formula (= ...)

top_layers.description: INHERITED: interface layers under the object — a count; or a formula (= ...)

bottom_layers.description: INHERITED: interface layers on what it stands on — a count; or a formula (= ...)

spacing.description: the gap between interface lines (0 = touching); unset = plymeld's rule, lines at bead contact — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

slot.description: the slot that prints support interface (0 = whichever is loaded) — a count; or a formula (= ...)

value.description: the gap between support's top and the object it holds up, rounded to whole layers; unset = one layer, at least gap.top.min — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

min.description: the least gap between support's top and the object when gap.top.value is unset: one layer, or as many as reach this (0.2 mm: 3 layers at 0.08 mm) — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

bottom.description: the gap between support standing on the model and the model's top under it; the support's lowest interface.bottom_layers above the gap are bottom interface, as on the bed; unset = one layer (the layer on the model's top left out); 0 = laid onto it — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

side.description: the gap beside the object, between support and the object's walls; unset = plymeld's rule, one support line — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

width.description: the narrowest column of support laid, so the narrowest overhang that gets support: an overhang is kept only where the overhang within this height above and below it, taken together, is at least this wide (a sloped face is a stack of thin strips, judged as a stack); what is narrower is a speck nothing could stand under and gets no support, a locked spot excepted; unset = plymeld's rule, a tree tip (two support lines) — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

spacing.description: INHERITED: gap between support lines — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

from_bed_only.description: INHERITED: only support standing on the bed — true or false; or a formula (= ...)

width.description: INHERITED: support line width — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

angle.description: INHERITED: support line direction — a angle (deg); or a formula (= ...)

slot.description: the slot that prints support (0 = whichever is loaded) — a count; or a formula (= ...)

branch_diameter.description: INHERITED: largest branch diameter — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

widening.description: INHERITED: how fast a branch widens going down — a angle (deg); or a formula (= ...)

tip_spacing.description: INHERITED: spacing of the tips under an overhang — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

min.description: a support spot the plan locks (what `plymeld plan -o` wrote of the search's choice): the faces too steep to hold themselves up within the box get tree support, nothing else does; the box's least corner: x and y from the posed object's corner (its least x and y), z from the object's bottom as posed — a point, x y z and a unit ("10 20 5 mm"); or an array of 3 numbers (mm)

max.description: the locked support spot's greatest corner (above min on x and y, at or above it on z: a flat underside), in the same frame — a point, x y z and a unit ("10 20 5 mm"); or an array of 3 numbers (mm)

order.description: the print order of the spot's support column beside the model's layers: interleaved = layer by layer with them; first = the column finished before the model's layers beside it start (only where it stays under the nozzle tip's protrusion, hardware.tool.<key>.head.nozzle.height). Unset = interleaved

min.description: a planned insert: a socket the print pauses at so an object is placed in it, the layer over it printed onto the object's top (no bridge, no support in the socket); the box's least corner, in the model's own coordinates; the pose must be locked (plan.pose = "as-given" or plan.object.<key>.pose.turn) and keep the socket opening upward — a point, x y z and a unit ("10 20 5 mm"); or an array of 3 numbers (mm)

max.description: the insert's box's greatest corner (above min on every axis), in the model's own coordinates — a point, x y z and a unit ("10 20 5 mm"); or an array of 3 numbers (mm)

top.description: the insert's top once placed, in the model's own z (unset: the box's top, max's z): the pause comes before the first layer whose bottom is at or above it, and that layer's bottom over the socket is laid onto the insert — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

top_order.description: the order of a curved band's top surface lines: one_way (unset) = one sweep across the surface, as any top, so on one side of a peak each new line goes down beside the one before, below it; uphill = the lines split where the surface is highest, each side laid from its lowest line up to it, so each new line goes down beside the one before on its low side (plate 8's solid arch came out rough on the half its top was swept down)

height.description: flat layers: the layer height where they keep one height (and of the flat layers under a curved band or holding up a lifted bridge); decided by the search over the tool's thinnest to thickest layer unless set in a config (the bundled value is only the stand-in other values are worked out from) — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

max.description: flat layers following the surfaces: the deepest stair-step a layer may leave (unset: the layer height) — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

height_ratio.description: the transition between layer heights: no layer (after the first) more than this much thicker than the one below it, and the layers before a band whose layers start thinner stepping down by about this much each ("1.5": a 0.08 mm band meets a 0.28 mm one through 0.12, 0.18, 0.27); "0" = no limit, a jump at the band's boundary — a multiplier (0.15 or 15%); or a formula (= ...)

layers.description: the hidden core in thicker layers: every this many layers, the sparse infill those layers share is laid once, on the last of them, the layers' height thick (within the tool's thickest layer); each layer's sparse infill outside what the group shares is laid on its own layer. "1" = every layer its own (off). Bundled: as many layers as fit the tool's thickest layer — a count; or a formula (= ...)

heights.description: how flat layers set their heights: one = one layer height for the whole object; follow = every layer as thick as the surfaces it crosses allow (needs the tool's thinnest and thickest layer, and no fuzzy skin); derive (or unset) = the search weighs both, and the bands flat layers' survey proposes (following the surfaces there, one height elsewhere)

fan.description: bond-first cooling's part fan for the object's lines; bundled half the filament's cooling.fan, a placeholder — a multiplier (0.15 or 15%); or a formula (= ...)

min.description: bond-first cooling's minimum layer time; bundled half the filament's, a placeholder — a time (s); or a formula (= ...)

temperature.description: bond-first cooling's nozzle temperature after the first layer, capped at the filament's temperature.max where set; bundled the filament's print temperature + 10 C, a placeholder — a temperature (C); or a formula (= ...)

ramp_speeds.description: an ARCHED lifted bridge's speeds over air in its layers after its first: its first layer's segments over the hollow at bridge.print.speed, the next layers' at these speeds in turn, in mm/s separated by commas (e.g. "6, 8, 12, 24 mm/s"), then each bridge.ramp_growth times the last, every one capped at the bridge speed (plan.mechanism.motion.bridge.speed), the ramp ending with the first that reaches it; the usual speeds after. Every segment over what holds the bridge up at the usual speeds throughout. Empty with ramp_growth "1" = no ramp: the usual speeds from the second layer. After a wave overhang's layer (its beads at wave_overhang.speed), the layers over the beads take the bridge's whole sequence: bridge.print.speed, then these, then the growth

ramp_growth.description: after bridge.ramp_speeds, each layer's speed over air of an ARCHED lifted bridge this many times the last, up to the bridge speed; "1" or less = no growth: the usual speeds after the listed ones — a multiplier (0.15 or 15%); or a formula (= ...)

temperature.description: the nozzle temperature of an ARCHED lifted bridge's own layers (its first layer arching above or below straight between its supports by more than half a layer: an arch, a sag; not a flat, ramp, or valley bridge), waited for before them; the rest of the object (what holds the bridge up) at its print temperature, waited for again after; over plan.mechanism.temperature.print and the filament's. Unset: the print temperature — a temperature (C); or a formula (= ...)

speed.description: an ARCHED lifted bridge's first layer, where it is over air (tacks too), at this speed, its next layers stepping up to the bridge speed as bridge.ramp_speeds and ramp_growth say; what lies over the bridge's supports at the usual speeds: no slow-down for layer time, no floor, no overhang grading on the slow segments (the melt cap still applies: it only lowers a speed when the filament cannot melt fast enough). Unset: the usual speeds — a speed (mm/s); or a formula (= ...)

every head move that extrudes nothing in an ARCHED lifted bridge's layers (travels, lifts, the drops into tacks) at most this fast; not retractions and their restores, which keep the filament's speeds. Unset: the usual speeds — a speed (mm/s); or a formula (= ...)

fill_angles.description: the direction of a lifted bridge's fill from its first layer up (its bottom, solid, sparse, and top fill): span (unset) = at its span's direction (as its first layer's bridge lines take it between its anchors) and at right angles to it, layer by layer, counted from its top so its top layer runs along the span, foot to foot; a grid's or cubic's sparse families from the span; object = the object's own fill directions (plan.layer.infill.angle, turned 90 deg layer by layer). With fill_along = true every fill but the top runs along the span either way

fill_along.description: a lifted bridge's layers all along its bridge: from its first layer up, every fill (bottom, solid) at the angle its first layer's bridge lines take; its top surface keeps its usual angle ("Allow for non-parallel motion on the top/finishing layers") — true or false; or a formula (= ...)

height.description: a lifted bridge's own layer height, for an object with several lifted bridges (each printed after the layer it rests on): what holds them up keeps the object's layer height (the double helix's wall at 0.1 mm, its arches at 0.2). Unset: the object's layer height. A lone lifted bridge shares the object's layers: a different value is refused — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

top_layer.description: an ARCHED lifted bridge's top layer (its last, when it has more than one): normal = at the usual speeds and the print temperature (waited for), ironing with it; bridge = at the bridge's own speeds and temperature, as its other layers

first_layer.description: a lifted bridge's first layer: lines (unset) = bridge lines from support to support; wave_overhang = wave beads (plan.technique.wave_overhang's spacing, overlap, line area, and speed) grown from every support at once over the whole span, each bead climbing from its support once lifted onto an arch, one support's side whole and then the other's, meeting where they are equally far from both (the peak of a symmetric arch); its layers above as the bridge's others

sides.description: the order of a waved first layer's sides (plan.technique.bridge.first_layer = wave_overhang): one_then_other (unset) = one support's side whole, then the other's; alternate = front by front, each front's beads on one side and then on the other, so neither side reaches out alone while the other is laid (every bead still climbs from its own support, and each side's edge beads come last); one_support = the fronts grow from one support only (the first in order of x then y) across the whole span, climbing to the peak and descending to the other support

order.description: when a waved first layer's edge pieces (its beads along the span's edges, each from its support up to the middle) are laid: with_each_side (unset) = after that side's beads across; last = after every bead across on both sides (with wave.sides = alternate they come last either way)

enabled.description: whether a waved first layer's edge pieces are laid at all: false = the beads across end at the span's edges; unset = laid — true or false; or a formula (= ...)

direction.description: which edge a waved first layer's beads across the span start from: mirrored (unset) = as grown, each side's beads from one edge, the two sides from opposite edges; matched = every bead from the same edge of the span; zigzag = as matched, every other front's beads from the other edge, so the starts and ends spread over both edges

crossing.description: how the head travels between a waved first layer's beads across the span: over (unset) = straight, above the bridge; beside = between the sides (wave.sides = alternate), out past the span's edge by wave.crossing_clearance, along it, and back in, so ooze on the way does not land on the bridge; away = after every bead across the span, out along the bead's own direction to wave.away.distance from the object (its outline seen from above, as a box), round the object at that distance the shorter way, and in to the next bead's start along that bead's direction, so the hot head is far from the beads between them; a wait (wave.wait, wave.wait_zones) is spent at the far point. The way round is not checked against the other objects on the plate: lay them out clear of it

distance.description: how far from the object the head goes after each bead with wave.crossing = away; unset there is an error — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

wait_zones.description: waits after the beads across the span that vary along it, over wave.wait: zones of the span from the first support (in order of x then y) to the second, in percent, each with its wait, separated by commas (e.g. "0-40%: 5 s, 40-60%: 10 s, 60-100%: 0 s"); a bead takes the wait of the zone its middle lies in, spent before the next bead (at the far point with wave.crossing = away, else lifted over the next bead's start); the last bead waits none. Unset = wave.wait after every bead

zones.description: a waved first layer's lines across the span laid a second time over it, after the whole layer, where zones of the span say (unset = none): zones from the first support (in order of x then y) to the second, in percent of the gap between them, each with how far above the first pass its lines are laid and their plastic as a share of the first pass's, separated by commas (e.g. "25-40%: 0.1 mm 50%, 40-60%: 0 mm 100%, 60-75%: 0.1 mm 50%"); a line belongs to the zone its middle lies in, and runs the other way to the line under it; the lines from the zones' outer ends inward, the two sides in turn, a line at the middle last; no edge pieces; at wave.second_pass.speed, each travel straight, lifted, and each line's start reached straight down from wave.second_pass.approach above it

speed.description: the speed of a waved first layer's second pass (wave.second_pass.zones); unset there is an error — a speed (mm/s); or a formula (= ...)

approach.description: how far above each line's start of a waved first layer's second pass the head comes straight down from (wave.second_pass.zones); unset there is an error — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

enabled.description: Xs over a waved first layer, laid after the whole layer (its edge pieces too): the span in sections of wave.x_length from each support, the one at the middle taking what is left of both sides; each X corner to corner between its section's first and last lines across the span, its ends wave.x_layer.inset in from the span's edges, wave.x_layer.raise above the layer at wave.x_layer.share of its lines' plastic; the two sides in turn from the supports to the middle, the middle X last; at wave.x_layer.speed. Needs a span between two supports and wave.spacing = even; unset = none — true or false; or a formula (= ...)

raise.description: how far above a waved first layer's top its Xs are laid (wave.x_layer.enabled; the X's line its own height under that); unset there is an error — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

share.description: the Xs' plastic per mm as a share of the waved first layer's lines' (wave.x_layer.enabled); unset there is an error — a multiplier (0.15 or 15%); or a formula (= ...)

inset.description: how far in from the span's edges each X's ends stop (wave.x_layer.enabled); unset there is an error — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

middle.description: when the X over the middle of a waved first layer's Xs is laid (wave.x_layer.enabled): last (unset) = after the sides' Xs; first = before them, the sides' then from the supports inward as before

speed.description: the speed of the Xs over a waved first layer (wave.x_layer.enabled); unset there is an error — a speed (mm/s); or a formula (= ...)

enabled.description: a full layer of lines along the span over a waved first layer, laid after it (and after its Xs, wave.x_layer): from support to support over the gap, at the solid fill's width and spacing (plan.layer.solid.line.width) across the gap's width, each the other way to the one before, wave.span_layer.raise above the waved layer's top, at wave.span_layer.speed and the solid fill's plastic. Needs a span between two supports and wave.spacing = even; unset = none — true or false; or a formula (= ...)

raise.description: how far above a waved first layer's top its layer of lines along the span is laid (wave.span_layer.enabled; the line's own height under that), at most two layers; unset there is an error — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

fan.description: bond-first cooling's part fan for the object's lines; bundled half the filament's cooling.fan, a placeholder — a multiplier (0.15 or 15%); or a formula (= ...)

min.description: bond-first cooling's minimum layer time; bundled half the filament's, a placeholder — a time (s); or a formula (= ...)

temperature.description: bond-first cooling's nozzle temperature after the first layer, capped at the filament's temperature.max where set; bundled the filament's print temperature + 10 C, a placeholder — a temperature (C); or a formula (= ...)

ramp_speeds.description: an ARCHED lifted bridge's speeds over air in its layers after its first: its first layer's segments over the hollow at bridge.print.speed, the next layers' at these speeds in turn, in mm/s separated by commas (e.g. "6, 8, 12, 24 mm/s"), then each bridge.ramp_growth times the last, every one capped at the bridge speed (plan.mechanism.motion.bridge.speed), the ramp ending with the first that reaches it; the usual speeds after. Every segment over what holds the bridge up at the usual speeds throughout. Empty with ramp_growth "1" = no ramp: the usual speeds from the second layer. After a wave overhang's layer (its beads at wave_overhang.speed), the layers over the beads take the bridge's whole sequence: bridge.print.speed, then these, then the growth

ramp_growth.description: after bridge.ramp_speeds, each layer's speed over air of an ARCHED lifted bridge this many times the last, up to the bridge speed; "1" or less = no growth: the usual speeds after the listed ones — a multiplier (0.15 or 15%); or a formula (= ...)

temperature.description: the nozzle temperature of an ARCHED lifted bridge's own layers (its first layer arching above or below straight between its supports by more than half a layer: an arch, a sag; not a flat, ramp, or valley bridge), waited for before them; the rest of the object (what holds the bridge up) at its print temperature, waited for again after; over plan.mechanism.temperature.print and the filament's. Unset: the print temperature — a temperature (C); or a formula (= ...)

speed.description: an ARCHED lifted bridge's first layer, where it is over air (tacks too), at this speed, its next layers stepping up to the bridge speed as bridge.ramp_speeds and ramp_growth say; what lies over the bridge's supports at the usual speeds: no slow-down for layer time, no floor, no overhang grading on the slow segments (the melt cap still applies: it only lowers a speed when the filament cannot melt fast enough). Unset: the usual speeds — a speed (mm/s); or a formula (= ...)

every head move that extrudes nothing in an ARCHED lifted bridge's layers (travels, lifts, the drops into tacks) at most this fast; not retractions and their restores, which keep the filament's speeds. Unset: the usual speeds — a speed (mm/s); or a formula (= ...)

fill_angles.description: the direction of a lifted bridge's fill from its first layer up (its bottom, solid, sparse, and top fill): span (unset) = at its span's direction (as its first layer's bridge lines take it between its anchors) and at right angles to it, layer by layer, counted from its top so its top layer runs along the span, foot to foot; a grid's or cubic's sparse families from the span; object = the object's own fill directions (plan.layer.infill.angle, turned 90 deg layer by layer). fill_along.description: a lifted bridge's layers all along its bridge: from its first layer up, every fill (bottom, solid) at the angle its first layer's bridge lines take; its top surface keeps its usual angle ("Allow for non-parallel motion on the top/finishing layers") — true or false; or a formula (= ...)

height.description: a lifted bridge's own layer height, for an object with several lifted bridges (each printed after the layer it rests on): what holds them up keeps the object's layer height (the double helix's wall at 0.1 mm, its arches at 0.2). Unset: the object's layer height. A lone lifted bridge shares the object's layers: a different value is refused — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

top_layer.description: an ARCHED lifted bridge's top layer (its last, when it has more than one): normal = at the usual speeds and the print temperature (waited for), ironing with it; bridge = at the bridge's own speeds and temperature, as its other layers

first_layer.description: a lifted bridge's first layer: lines (unset) = bridge lines from support to support; wave_overhang = wave beads (plan.technique.wave_overhang's spacing, overlap, line area, and speed) grown from every support at once over the whole span, each bead climbing from its support once lifted onto an arch, one support's side whole and then the other's, meeting where they are equally far from both (the peak of a symmetric arch); its layers above as the bridge's others

sides.description: the order of a waved first layer's sides (plan.technique.bridge.first_layer = wave_overhang): one_then_other (unset) = one support's side whole, then the other's; alternate = front by front, each front's beads on one side and then on the other, so neither side reaches out alone while the other is laid (every bead still climbs from its own support, and each side's edge beads come last); one_support = the fronts grow from one support only (the first in order of x then y) across the whole span, climbing to the peak and descending to the other support

order.description: when a waved first layer's edge pieces (its beads along the span's edges, each from its support up to the middle) are laid: with_each_side (unset) = after that side's beads across; last = after every bead across on both sides (with wave.sides = alternate they come last either way)

enabled.description: whether a waved first layer's edge pieces are laid at all: false = the beads across end at the span's edges; unset = laid — true or false; or a formula (= ...)

direction.description: which edge a waved first layer's beads across the span start from: mirrored (unset) = as grown, each side's beads from one edge, the two sides from opposite edges; matched = every bead from the same edge of the span; zigzag = as matched, every other front's beads from the other edge, so the starts and ends spread over both edges

crossing.description: how the head travels between a waved first layer's beads across the span: over (unset) = straight, above the bridge; beside = between the sides (wave.sides = alternate), out past the span's edge by wave.crossing_clearance, along it, and back in, so ooze on the way does not land on the bridge; away = after every bead across the span, out along the bead's own direction to wave.away.distance from the object (its outline seen from above, as a box), round the object at that distance the shorter way, and in to the next bead's start along that bead's direction, so the hot head is far from the beads between them; a wait (wave.wait, wave.wait_zones) is spent at the far point. distance.description: how far from the object the head goes after each bead with wave.crossing = away; unset there is an error — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

wait_zones.description: waits after the beads across the span that vary along it, over wave.wait: zones of the span from the first support (in order of x then y) to the second, in percent, each with its wait, separated by commas (e.g. "0-40%: 5 s, 40-60%: 10 s, 60-100%: 0 s"); a bead takes the wait of the zone its middle lies in, spent before the next bead (at the far point with wave.crossing = away, else lifted over the next bead's start); the last bead waits none. zones.description: a waved first layer's lines across the span laid a second time over it, after the whole layer, where zones of the span say (unset = none): zones from the first support (in order of x then y) to the second, in percent of the gap between them, each with how far above the first pass its lines are laid and their plastic as a share of the first pass's, separated by commas (e.g. "25-40%: 0.1 mm 50%, 40-60%: 0 mm 100%, 60-75%: 0.1 mm 50%"); a line belongs to the zone its middle lies in, and runs the other way to the line under it; the lines from the zones' outer ends inward, the two sides in turn, a line at the middle last; no edge pieces; at wave.second_pass.speed, each travel straight, lifted, and each line's start reached straight down from wave.second_pass.approach above it

speed.description: the speed of a waved first layer's second pass (wave.second_pass.zones); unset there is an error — a speed (mm/s); or a formula (= ...)

approach.description: how far above each line's start of a waved first layer's second pass the head comes straight down from (wave.second_pass.zones); unset there is an error — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

enabled.description: Xs over a waved first layer, laid after the whole layer (its edge pieces too): the span in sections of wave.x_length from each support, the one at the middle taking what is left of both sides; each X corner to corner between its section's first and last lines across the span, its ends wave.x_layer.inset in from the span's edges, wave.x_layer.raise above the layer at wave.x_layer.share of its lines' plastic; the two sides in turn from the supports to the middle, the middle X last; at wave.x_layer.speed. raise.description: how far above a waved first layer's top its Xs are laid (wave.x_layer.enabled; the X's line its own height under that); unset there is an error — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

share.description: the Xs' plastic per mm as a share of the waved first layer's lines' (wave.x_layer.enabled); unset there is an error — a multiplier (0.15 or 15%); or a formula (= ...)

inset.description: how far in from the span's edges each X's ends stop (wave.x_layer.enabled); unset there is an error — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

middle.description: when the X over the middle of a waved first layer's Xs is laid (wave.x_layer.enabled): last (unset) = after the sides' Xs; first = before them, the sides' then from the supports inward as before

speed.description: the speed of the Xs over a waved first layer (wave.x_layer.enabled); unset there is an error — a speed (mm/s); or a formula (= ...)

enabled.description: a full layer of lines along the span over a waved first layer, laid after it (and after its Xs, wave.x_layer): from support to support over the gap, at the solid fill's width and spacing (plan.layer.solid.line.width) across the gap's width, each the other way to the one before, wave.span_layer.raise above the waved layer's top, at wave.span_layer.speed and the solid fill's plastic. Needs a span between two supports and wave.spacing = even; unset = none — true or false; or a formula (= ...)

raise.description: how far above a waved first layer's top its layer of lines along the span is laid (wave.span_layer.enabled; the line's own height under that), at most two layers; unset there is an error — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

speed.description: the speed of the layer of lines along the span over a waved first layer (wave.span_layer.enabled); unset there is an error — a speed (mm/s); or a formula (= ...)

spacing.description: how a waved first layer's lines are spaced along the span: as_grown (unset) = each front wave_overhang.spacing on from the last, as measured from above, the two sides' last lines left with whatever space remains between them; even = the span from each support's first line to the other's divided into an even number of equal steps, as near wave_overhang.spacing as can be, measured along the bridge's surface (an arch's slopes as well as its top), so the lines lie equally far apart all along it and there is an odd number of them: each side's from its support, and one in the middle, laid after both sides' lines (with wave.line.direction = zigzag running the other way to both sides' last lines); each line straight across the span between its edges. Needs a span between two supports, wave.layers = 1, wave.start = whole and wave.front = straight; with wave.sides = one_support it does not apply

crossing_clearance.description: how far past the span's edge the head goes on a crossing beside the bridge (wave.crossing = beside); plymeld's bundled value is a placeholder — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

retract.description: the retraction before each travel between a waved first layer's beads, over the filament's retract.length (unset = the filament's) — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

wipe.description: whether the head wipes along the bead it has just laid while retracting before each travel between a waved first layer's beads, over the filament's retract.wipe.enabled (unset = the filament's); the wipe's distance, speed, and share as the filament's — true or false; or a formula (= ...)

wait.description: a wait before each bead of a waved first layer but its first, the head lifted over the bead's start (unset = none): more time for the bead before to cool — a time (s); or a formula (= ...)

layers.description: how many of a lifted bridge's first layers are laid as waves (plan.technique.bridge.first_layer = wave_overhang): 1 (unset) = the first; 2 = the first two together, the second's beads the first's fronts one layer up, laid one front behind the first's on each side in turn, so the second layer lands only where the first already reaches one front further out (needs wave.sides = alternate)

second_layer.description: with two waved layers (wave.layers = 2), the second: full (unset) = every front, laid one front behind the first's; x = only an X over each section of the first layer (wave.x_length along the span), its two diagonals corner to corner from the section's first front's ends to its last front's, laid on each side as soon as the first layer covers its whole section; the sections run from each support, and the one at the middle, over where the sides meet, takes what is left of both sides (at least one section): the X's triangles stay open, and the rest of that layer over the gap is left to them but for the strip's edges, laid as on a full second layer (needs two supports, each front one line across)

x_length.description: how far along the span each X of a waved second layer reaches (wave.second_layer = x), rounded to whole fronts (wave_overhang.spacing apart; at least two); unset with wave.second_layer = x is an error — a length (mm); or a formula (= ...)

start.description: the region a waved first layer lays first, as it lays a whole span (wave.sides, wave.line.direction, wave.crossing as set), before the rest of the span is filled with waves grown from the supports and from what was laid, front by front: whole (unset) = the whole span, nothing after; edge_strips = a strip wave.strip.width wide along each edge of the span, support to support; triangles = from each support a triangle as wide as the span there, narrowing to a point at the middle of one edge, the two meeting there; opposite_triangles = as triangles, the second support's point on the other edge.
